title: add hierarchical toolflow schematic and minimal authoring snippets
author: Daniel Park
release_notes: Add a compact hierarchical toolflow schematic and three minimal authoring snippets for quick onboarding. No runtime changes. Docs-only release.
body: Context: We've seen authors struggle to express multi-step tool-calling flows (nested tool calls, conditional tool routing, and retry semantics) using flat examples. This PR introduces a compact hierarchical toolflow schematic and three minimal authoring snippets (CLI starter, browser shim, and CI smoke scenario) to make nested toolflow patterns easier to author and troubleshoot. Motivation: improve onboarding for new authors, reduce cognitive load when composing agents that call tools that themselves call other tools, and provide a small, runnable example that can be executed locally and in CI. Changes: added a new authoring guide (docs/authoring/hierarchical-toolflow.md), a visual ASCII schematic used in the docs (docs/authoring/assets/toolflow-schematic.txt), three runnable example folders under examples/toolflow-ministarter/{cli,browser,ci-smoke} with lightweight adapters and README walkthroughs, and a short tests harness (examples/toolflow-ministarter/tests/run_smoke.py) used by CI to validate the shape of outputs. Implementation notes: examples are intentionally minimal (no external infra), rely on the existing local dev shim in examples/common/shim, and include telemetry probe points documented in the authoring guide. Checklist: [x] authoring guide written and proofread, [x] runnable snippets added, [x] CI smoke task added to docs pipeline, [x] add minimal telemetry probe examples, [ ] consider adding a TypeScript variant in a follow-up (linked ENG-3201). How to review: read docs/authoring/hierarchical-toolflow.md for rationale and examples, run the CLI snippet with `python examples/toolflow-ministarter/cli/run.py` and confirm the sample sequence and fallback behavior, run the CI smoke `python examples/toolflow-ministarter/tests/run_smoke.py` or check the CI result. Backwards compatibility: docs-only and examples; no API surface or runtime changes. Related: references ENG-3129 (authoring improvements) and PM-4581 (onboarding flow).
commits: 3 commits: 1) add hierarchical authoring guide and ascii schematic (authoring/hierarchical-toolflow.md + assets) || 2) add three minimal example runners and README walkthroughs (examples/toolflow-ministarter/*) || 3) add CI smoke harness and update docs pipeline (ci/docs-smoke-config)
files_snippets: docs/authoring/hierarchical-toolflow.md: includes a short worked example and a compact schematic. examples/toolflow-ministarter/cli/run.py: minimal runner that composes three tool calls where tool B may call tool C; includes retry-on-failure logic and emits telemetry probe events. examples/toolflow-ministarter/tests/run_smoke.py: asserts the sequence of tool invocations and that fallback was exercised.
review_thread: Priya Shah: Nice focused guide. Can you add a one-line note on telemetry retention and what the probe points emit? Requested change: add a small table mapping probe names to events.
Daniel Park (author): Added a telemetry mapping table at the end of the doc and annotated the CLI runner with probe names. Pushed commit to address comment.

Ethan Chen: The browser adapter stub uses a Promise-based API; can we clarify error propagation semantics so authors don't assume synchronous failures? Suggested change: add a short note in browser/README and a unit test for promise rejection path.
Daniel Park (author): Added rejection-path example and a tiny test in ci-smoke. PTAL.
Lena Gomez: Docs build failed initially due to site-toc.yaml ordering. CI now green. Approving changes.
Priya Shah: Approving after telemetry table addition.

notes: This PR intentionally keeps runtime changes out of scope. If adoption increases we'll promote the CLI example to a small tutorial with more robust adapters.
user_visible_summary: Adds a compact hierarchical toolflow authoring guide and three runnable starter snippets (CLI, browser, CI smoke) to help authors compose nested tool-calling flows. Docs-only change, merged to main.
